items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: I think you might remember him as being Ray Robinson's second.

ctx.x: And well, I know 101 Ranch closed and me and Eddie Durham was all tight, we hit it off together, we were a team, and we used to play our gigs together and get our little riffs together and then we started creeping over to New York. At that time the dancing schools were in vogue, so we're going to dancing school and set the dancing school on fire, we would get a job.

But then they started saying we can't have no trombone, got to use the trumpet (unintelligible) so we used that particular pattern for quite some time and then Eddie, I think he left and went west and then I come to New York and now the first place I went was to New York, I went to Small's Paradise and Teddy Hill, I think was playing the saxophone. A fellow named June Clark, a great trumpet player. I think you might remember him as being Ray Robinson's second. He and Sonny Greer grew up together. Their fathers…
